results.title: LPC-transformer: a training strategy optimized framework for multiclass pneumonia medical image classification
results.text_preview: The Swin-Transformer (20) model, based on windowing, multi-level feature interaction, and a hierarchical attention mechanism, can simultaneously capture both global and local features in medical images and fuse them together. This model uses convolution operations to segment medical images into small patches and project them into high-dimensional vectors, thereby dividing the feature maps into windows. The feature map vectors undergo sequential processing across four stages. Except for the first stage, which performs linear embedding, the remaining stages first perform patch merging and downsampling on adjacent feature map windows, after which the feature map vectors are fed into a Swin-Transformer block for processing. This experiment uses 224 × 224 × 1 lung medical image feature maps (21); the complete processing workflow and the feature map vectors at each stage are shown in Figure 3.
